findings.title: retryCount deletion branch not scoped to SMS method
findings.body: The new OR clause `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` in the deleteMany call has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the first clause. Since `retryCount` is a shared column on the `WorkflowReminder` model used for all methods (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP), any non-SMS reminder that somehow ends up with retryCount > 1 (e.g. via future code reuse of this field, or a bug elsewhere) would be silently deleted regardless of method. This widens the deletion scope beyond what the PR intends (deleting failed SMS reminders) and can cause data loss for unrelated reminder types.

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment is racy
findings.body: retryCount is incremented by reading the in-memory `reminder.retryCount` value fetched at the start of the loop and writing `reminder.retryCount + 1` back. This is not atomic: if this cron job overlaps with another run (or is retried concurrently), both executions could read the same stale value and write the same incremented result, losing an increment. Using Prisma's atomic `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` would avoid this race and ensure the failure count is accurate, which matters since after retryCount > 1 the reminder is permanently deleted.

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment is racy (catch block)
findings.body: Same issue as the success-path update: `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }` computes the new value from a value read earlier in this request rather than using an atomic increment. Concurrent executions of this cron handler could under-count failures, delaying or preventing the intended deletion of permanently-failing SMS reminders after two failures.

findings.title: retryCount never incremented when message/sendTo is missing
findings.body: If `message` ends up empty/null or `sendTo` is falsy, the `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)` branch is skipped entirely and neither the success path nor the new retryCount-increment path executes. Such a reminder will be re-fetched by every subsequent cron run (scheduled remains false) but its retryCount will never increase, so it will never hit the new retryCount>1 deletion condition. This defeats the purpose of the fix for this class of failure (e.g. workflowStep with no body and no recognized template, or missing sendTo), leaving the reminder stuck forever instead of being retried/deleted.

findings.title: Stale comment not updated for new deletion logic
findings.body: The comment above the deleteMany call still reads "delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date", but the query was changed to also delete any reminder (not necessarily SMS, not necessarily past its scheduled date) that has retryCount > 1. The comment should be updated to describe the new OR condition so maintainers understand the full deletion criteria.

findings.title: No automated test coverage for new retry logic
findings.body: This PR introduces new behavior (incrementing retryCount on failure, and deleting reminders once retryCount > 1) but no tests were added or updated to verify: (1) that retryCount increments on a twilio.scheduleSMS failure/exception, (2) that reminders with retryCount > 1 are deleted on the next run, and (3) that successful scheduling does not affect retryCount. Given this directly affects whether customer SMS reminders are silently dropped, test coverage would help prevent regressions.
